summary: Public functions for adding inflection rules, irregular words and uncountable words at runtime, so applications stop editing the module's tables by hand.
behaviour: `inflection.plural(rule, replacement)` and `inflection.singular(rule, replacement)` add a pluralization or singularization rule. `rule` is a regular expression string and `replacement` its `re.sub` replacement, as in the built-in tables. The newest rule is tried first, before rules added earlier and before the built-in rules.

`inflection.irregular(singular, plural)` registers an irregular word in both directions and keeps the case of its first letter (`Octopus` becomes `Octopuses`). A word registered as irregular, in either form, is no longer uncountable.
`inflection.uncountable(*words)` makes each word uncountable: `pluralize` and `singularize` return it unchanged, whatever case it is written in and whatever case it was registered in.
The built-in rules and words keep working as they do on main.
history: - Fixed: Type hints for every public function.

entries: - Added: `__all__` lists the public functions, so `from inflection import *` imports only those. (feature/c3f58a)
- Changed: The rule tables hold compiled patterns, so pluralize and singularize no longer compile a pattern on every call. (feature/91c4ae)
